correctness.rationale: Concavity of λ₂ in conductances and S_s×S_r averaging guarantee an orbit-constant global optimum. The exact spectrum is 0, sa+rb (mult s−1), sb+rc (mult r−1), (s+r)b; hence λ₂=min(sa+rb,sb+rc,(s+r)b). The normalized gap-one reciprocal budget reduces to F_t(b)=sr b+[t(s−1)/2](1−rb)_++[(r−1)/2](1−sb)_+ on b≥1/(s+r). Its piecewise slopes change sign at τ1=s(r+1)/(r(s−1)) and, when s>r, τ2=2s/(s−1). Minimizers b=1/n,1/r for s≤r or b=1/n,1/s,1/r for s>r give all printed rates/gaps. Slopes vanish across stated boundary intervals, explaining nonunique orbit-constant transition optimizers. Independent exact rational Laplacian eigenchecks and breakpoint/LP checks validated s,r≤6 across price branches. No arbitrary-optimum uniqueness is claimed.

originality.rationale: The continuous-time spectral-gap budget SDP and group-invariant reduction are classical (Sun et al. 2006, Boyd et al. 2009); they receive no novelty credit. The closed two-price threshold law and counterintuitive middle phase deleting cheap B-internal edges while retaining expensive A-internal ones require the specific 3-variable eigenspace/LP analysis, not the statement of a general SDP. Interconnected-network spectral transitions optimize a different edge set. No matching earlier exact priced-clique theorem was located; residual specialized-prior risk remains.

value.rationale: An exact optimizer is a natural solution of the fastest-mixing allocation problem; the two thresholds show a nontrivial topological design transition, including an unintuitive support change that generic SDP numerical solvability does not explain. The formulas apply uniformly to all integer block sizes and positive price t, so this is a structural optimization classification rather than a chosen example.
